title: On the continuity of conditional distributions and stratification for derivative pricing
abstract: arXiv:2610.32970v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Stratification can reduce the estimator variance in Monte Carlo simulations by partitioning the sample space according to a low-dimensional factor and sampling separately within the resulting strata, making it well suited to the valuation of path-dependent claims in high-dimensional financial models. Its performance, however, depends critically on the choice of the stratification factor, and effective low-dimensional factors are generally difficult to identify in complex continuous-time models. Neural networks provide a flexible approximation class for this purpose and have proved useful in related variance-reduction problems in quantitative finance. In this paper, we study the construction of neural stratification factors for derivative pricing under proportional allocation in continuous-time models. translated_title: 论条件分布的连续性与衍生品定价中的分层方法
translated_abstract: 分层方法可以通过依据一个低维因子对样本空间进行划分，并在所得到的各个层内分别进行采样，从而降低蒙特卡洛模拟中估计量的方差，因此非常适合于高维金融模型中路径依赖型衍生品的估值。然而，其性能在很大程度上取决于分层因子的选择，而在复杂的连续时间模型中，有效的低维因子通常难以识别。神经网络为此提供了一类灵活的近似工具，并且已在量化金融中相关的方差缩减问题上被证明是有用的。本文研究了在连续时间模型下，按比例分配进行衍生品定价时神经分层因子的构造问题。由于分层因子的数值构造通常涉及近似处理，我们为相关条件分布建立了连续性结果。
tldr: 本文提出在连续时间模型下利用神经网络构造衍生品定价的分层因子，并通过建立条件分布的连续性结果来保证近似构造的合理性与有效性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes constructing neural stratification factors for derivative pricing in continuous-time models and establishes continuity results for conditional distributions to justify the numerical approximations involved.
